title: What If Every Mosquito on Earth Vanished Tonight?

scenes.text: What if every mosquito vanished tonight? The first number is the one that matters.
Mosquito-borne diseases are linked to more than 700,000 human deaths a year. Malaria alone killed about 608,000 people in 2022.
Only females bite. And of roughly 3,500 species, only about 40 are truly dangerous, because they spread disease.
Nature would lose a food source. Fish, frogs, dragonflies and birds all eat mosquitoes. But no bat species specializes in them.
Males live on nectar, and some pollinate orchids, though not as well as bees.
Many scientists suspect ecosystems would cope. Hundreds of thousands of families would feel the difference.
